title: What the Lineage Explorer is
description: The explorer answers 'where did this come from and what happened to it' for any data artifact: the sources, the transformations, the combinations, the reuses. It renders the full biography as a navigable graph, so auditors, scientists, and engineers can each follow the trail they care about.

title: Lineage event data model
description: Every transformation is an event record: inputs with identities, the operation with its code version and parameters, outputs with identities, the actor, and the timestamp. title: Lineage capture algorithm
description: Capture instruments pipelines automatically: wrapping transforms to emit events, fingerprinting inputs and outputs, and recording code versions. Manual steps get structured log forms. The goal is zero-effort capture for automated pipelines and low-effort capture for human steps — lineage nobody records is lineage nobody has.

description: Given any artifact, the assembler walks backward to raw sources and forward to all reuses, building the complete biography graph. It handles merges (many inputs, one output), splits, and cycles from iterative processes — and marks inferred steps distinctly from recorded ones.

title: Worked example: auditing a published figure
description: A published figure claims a 26.1 percent efficiency. The explorer traces it: from the figure to the analysis script version, to the cleaned dataset, to the raw instrument files, to the calibration certificates. One cleaning step used a superseded script — the audit flags it, the figure is recomputed with the current script, and the correction is published with the full trail.

title: Failure modes: dark pipelines and identity collisions
description: Lineage fails when pipelines go dark, when artifact identities collide, or when manual steps go unrecorded. Defenses: coverage dashboards with dark-pipeline alerts, content-based identity that survives renames, and mandatory capture gates before publication. Unrecorded history is treated as a defect with an owner and a deadline.

title: Security: lineage as sensitive metadata
description: Lineage reveals processes — who built what from what — which can be proprietary or sensitive. Lineage records carry access controls, sensitive operations are redacted to authorized roles, and the explorer audits every biography viewed. Transparency for auditors, privacy for builders, enforced by the same graph.
